It's November 14, 2026, and this is International News. The White House says Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold their first three-way summit in China next week, on the sidelines of APEC. Trump plans to discuss reducing nuclear weapons and the Iran war. In the United States, officials say the longest nationwide ground stop since 9/11 was caused by old equipment overloading, not a cyber-attack or a Microsoft outage. More than 1.5 million passengers faced disruption, including NBA, NHL and college football teams. Separately, Microsoft says it is deeply sorry for a global outage and reports a broad recovery. Experts call it a stark reminder of how heavily the world relies on a few big tech providers. The fallout from the Nvidia scandal is widening. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested Howard Lutnick's commerce department failed to ban chip exports to a firm thought to have links with China. The case has also put a spotlight on Singapore as a chip hub. And the FBI says North Korean hackers used fake video calls in a scheme called FaceStealer, stealing 400 million dollars in crypto from more than 900 victims over the last 18 months. That's International News for today.

Today is November 1st, 2026, and this is AI Tech News. Signs of strain are showing in AI finance. OpenAI has reportedly lowered the funding target for its new round, as the latest raise doesn't seem to be living up to expectations. Meanwhile, the Financial Times reports that Anthropic is expected to receive a high junk rating from credit agencies following its IPO, based on a Blackstone forecast. Such a rating would make it harder and costlier for Anthropic to raise money to fund its massive spending. In policy news, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that lets publishers opt out of AI scraping. Using a shared policy token signal, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple companies at once, instead of setting them individually. Apple announced that Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3. The features will appear first in a beta launching November 4th, with the full release scheduled for December. And finally, Google's AI chip equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. The company booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units, and the on-board Gemma 4 model wrote a haiku about being in space. That's all for today's AI Tech News. Thanks for listening.
